decision: Base UI + tailwind-variants slots, no hand-rolled primitives
why: session directive; Base UI 1.5.0 ships 48 primitives incl. useRender/merge-props

decision: Deleted hand-rolled spring/frame-clock/board-engine

result: removed before anything depended on them

decision: Router SPA, not TanStack Start

result: lab boots; route files stay Start-compatible

why: Base UI publishes --collapsible-panel-height; POC lesson 3 measured a JS height loop at ~25fps vs smooth as a CSS transition
result: collapse toggles; tween on the compositor

decision: pending tone dash tinted to accent/25
why: at #26302a the dash was invisible and the card read as finished, inverting its message

decision: Deleted src/geometry, lib/tv, lib/slot-class, lib/cn, components/widget

evidence: git rm; vp check 11 files clean
result: package is Base UI wrappers + tv slots only

decision: slotClass replaced by tv own className merging
why: tailwind-variants slot fns take className and merge with tailwind-merge; the helper duplicated it
result: no bespoke class joiner remains

decision: Separator vertical uses self-stretch + min-h floor
why: h-full collapses to zero in a row with no set height; the rule did not draw
result: not yet re-observed

decision: Corrected widget-runtime.md; it claimed deleted geometry survived as "genuinely ours"
why: the doc outlived the teardown and would have sent the next agent to files that do not exist
result: doc matches the tree; Base UI and motion surfaces recorded

decision: Added Switch, Slider, ScrollArea on Base UI parts
why: instrument controls a widget kit needs; parts read from index.parts.d.ts rather than guessed
result: render and interact in the showcase

decision: Mapped --radius-pk-pill into @theme inline
why: the token existed but was never exposed, so rounded-pk-pill was a silent no-op across chips, toggles, switch and slider thumb
result: observed: pills are pills; before/after screenshots differ

decision: Added Dialog, Popover, Menu with Content collapsing Portal+Positioner+Popup
why: the three share Base UI floating machinery; parts read from index.parts.d.ts
result: menu opens visibly; dialog and popover confirmed in DOM

decision: Menu.GroupLabel moved inside Menu.Group in the showcase
why: GroupLabel reads MenuGroupContext; outside Group it threw at open time, past typecheck
result: menu opens without error

decision: Ruled out the duplicate-React warning
why: console showed "more than one copy of React"; store has one react@19.2.7 and one react-dom, so it was HMR teardown during a broken intermediate state
result: no dependency fault

decision: Added Tabs and Toolbar
why: Tabs indicator uses Base UI active-tab CSS vars so the marker slides as one transition; Toolbar takes render so rail buttons stay the kit Button and it contributes only roving focus
result: tabs switch (DOM confirmed); toolbar renders as a pill rail

decision: Toolbar separator uses --pk-line not --pk-line-inner
why: inner is for a rule inside a card; on a raised rail it did not clear the fill and drew nothing
result: not yet re-observed

decision: This browser pane lags DOM updates in screenshots
why: dialog, popover and a tab switch all read as no-ops in a screenshot while present in the DOM; find/read_page is the reliable read
result: stop reading a stale screenshot as a defect

decision: Replaced the asserted contrast claim in theme.css with measured ratios
why: the comment said ink-dim and ink-faint are "the dimmest values that clear 4.5:1"; measured they are 4.95-5.88, above the floor, so the claim was not true and hid which pair is actually at risk
evidence: WCAG sRGB computation over the six inks against three grounds
result: ink-faint on surface is 4.95 at 10-11px, one step from failing; recorded rather than moved

decision: Recorded hairline separations as measured
why: line is 1.19:1 and line-inner 1.08:1 against surface; they are separations not contrasts, and line-inner vanishing on a raised surface explains the toolbar divider defect
result: explains why the toolbar separator needed --pk-line

decision: Added Accordion; Header and Trigger collapsed into one part
why: an accordion row has no arrangement where the two differ; panel uses --accordion-panel-height like Collapsible
result: renders as a ruled list; opens on click (DOM confirmed)

decision: Added group/row to the accordion trigger
why: the title slot used group-hover/row: with no element declaring the group, so that hover matched nothing
result: caught before commit, not observed live

decision: Planned Widget from counts instead of taste; recorded as docs/design/widget.md
why: two built-then-deleted attempts; the user reserved unplanned building, not planning
evidence: counted the POC: 45 widgets, 49 mono metadata, 15 sans labels, 14 uppercase kinds, 13 footers
result: the counts refute both attempts — no single Label, Footer is not a part, metadata is the through-line

decision: Built Surface + Row + the text vocabulary from docs/design/widget.md
why: the plan two turns ago; these are the parts with no open question attached
result: four surfaces render with label/kind/meta/title/prose/readout as authored

decision: Settled the open API question: role components AND an exported textVariants
why: Readout needs aria-live so it is a component regardless; exporting the tv fn covers elements the kit does not own, which is the same shape buttonVariants already has
result: one implementation, two entry points

decision: Row replaces Header/Body/Footer
why: several POC widgets put the naming line at the bottom and the printer has two, so Header asserted a structure the design lacks; rule=above carries the closing rule that Footer used to imply
result: second showcase card composes two Rows, one ruled

decision: Did NOT build Sparkline; built Bars instead
why: counted the POC: 5 canvases with 5 different painters (drawSpark, paintSweep, paintChart, weather, WebGPU) share nothing but the tag, while 24 bar children across 2 widgets share one exact shape
evidence: canvas refs fx/chart/spark/line + blobfx; height:30% children = 24
result: the abstraction that exists got built; the one that does not, did not

decision: Bars is DOM, not canvas
why: a height change is then a CSS transition on the compositor, and values survive a document producing no frames
result: two POC shapes (install bars, level columns) render from one component

decision: ActivityGrid on CSS Grid, not absolute pitch arithmetic
why: columns are weeks and rows are weekdays, so grid owns the pitch and nothing computes offsets; the POC computed every cell position by hand
result: 182 cells, first day lands on its correct weekday row, six month labels

decision: ResizeObserver moved from the grid to the root
why: the grid is sized by its own columns, so observing it feeds the measurement back into the layout that produced it — the loop the POC handoff warns about
result: typechecked; fitting NOT observed, see next row

decision: The week-fitting behaviour cannot be verified in this pane
why: document.hidden is true and a fresh independent ResizeObserver fired 0 callbacks while the observed element resized 518 to 198; matches the recorded hidden-pane hazard
result: stopped rewriting correct code against a broken instrument

decision: The primitive set is complete for what the design source demonstrates
why: counted the source: 48 widget definitions, 531 inline styles, zero classes, zero form inputs, 14 buttons, 5 canvases; what remains is bespoke widget instances and canvas painters, not reusable primitives
result: stopped adding components and built the site instead

decision: Avatar and a ping indicator are NOT components
why: each occurs exactly once in the design source; a round dot occurs 11 times but is three utilities, so wrapping it would be pure indirection
result: counting refuted all three before any code

decision: Base UI NavigationMenu is the wrong primitive for the component rail
why: its documented anatomy is Trigger plus Portal/Positioner/Popup for a horizontal menubar; a persistent index of pages has no disclosure to own
result: rail is a nav of router links; corrects an earlier note that named NavigationMenu

decision: Router owns which rail link is current
why: activeProps accepts data-* keys, so the router writes data-active and the tv variants read it; nothing compares pathnames
result: 7 routes walked by click, exactly one active link on each

decision: motionCharacter maps onto motion springs with no integrator
why: the design integrates v += (-K(x-target) - Cv)dt at unit mass, so k is stiffness and c is damping; snappy 340/30, balanced 220/26, floaty 130/18
result: recorded, not yet built: nothing in the kit needs a spring until a board exists

decision: Disabled on the accent tone drops the fill, not just the opacity
why: at 40% opacity a saturated fill is still the loudest control in the row, so a button that cannot be pressed read as the one to press; found by looking at the tone-by-size matrix
result: disabled accent now paints transparent on --pk-line with --pk-ink-faint, same reading as chip

decision: The accordion trigger carries a caret, superseding the row below that left this open
why: I had parked this as the owner's call, which was wrong — it is a component decision; the caret is ::after so a trigger is still just a title and a meta, drawn from two borders on a rotated square since the kit ships no icon set, and open turns it accent, the job theme.css already assigns the accent
result: open row shows an accent caret pointing up with its panel expanded, closed rows show faint carets down

decision: The accordion row treatment came from a list of links, not a disclosure
why: the design's writing widget is four a-href rows, ruled with a top hairline, title left and mono date right, hover to bright; that treatment is what Accordion wears, but a link needs no expand affordance and a disclosure trigger does, which is why the rows do not announce that they open
evidence: POC writing widget, 4 rows in 1 widget
result: left alone deliberately: the source has zero svg, so an indicator would invent an icon convention, and a link-list component would duplicate the accordion for one occurrence — worth a decision from the owner

decision: Reduced motion means no movement, not nothing happens
why: colour and opacity are not motion and carry the hover and pressed states, so they still cross-fade; anything that travels, scales, spins or opens by height snaps, and the two decorative infinite loops stop
result: forcing the query to match turns the switch thumb from transform/translate/scale/rotate into colour-only, while the button keeps its colour fade

decision: CollapsiblePanel owns the gap under its trigger, like AccordionPanel
why: the two panels had drifted: the accordion wrapped children in a spacing element and the collapsible left it to the caller, so the old showcase carried a pt-3 of its own; the padding goes on the wrapper because Base UI publishes the measured content height and a border-box panel would subtract it and clip the last line
result: body padding 12px, panel padding 0, client height 51 equals content 51 so nothing is cut

decision: The sizing rule is pinned by a test, not by a layout
why: the component reaches the rule through a ResizeObserver that needs a laid-out document, but the rule is a pure function of width and needs nothing; a second attempt to observe it in the pane also failed, root 501 to 278 with the cell count unchanged
result: 8 tests; breaking drop-weeks fails 3 and breaking the padding fails 2

decision: The month strip shares a grid column with the cells
why: its offsets are measured from the plot origin but it spanned the root, so every label sat 34px — the weekday column plus its gap — left of the week it named; sep pointed into August
result: all six labels measure 0px from the first cell of their month; 182 cells unchanged

decision: Hairline specimens are a fixed length
why: each rule was sized by the caption beside it, so the four samples spanned 231-329px and the lightest drew the longest, implying a magnitude the set has none of
result: all four measure 220px, four distinct colours

decision: Relatedness is depth, not opacity
why: the design moves related widgets to a forward plane and pushes the rest back, with a note that dimming alone flattened the board into one grey wash
result: constrains the future focus treatment

decision: The props table is read off each component's own tv object
why: a hand-kept list of variants is wrong the first time a variant is added; tv already carries variants and defaultVariants, so the table cannot drift
result: button, surface, row and bars each show their variants with the default marked

decision: No props table for ToggleGroup or Switch
why: their pressed and checked variants are state Base UI hands to className, not consumer props, and a table built from the object alone cannot tell those apart
result: omitted rather than inventing two props that do not exist

decision: The layout page shows all seven surface tones
why: its own header claimed seven while four were on the page and two more were only on the overview
result: card, sunken, deep, tile, rim, pending and bare all render

decision: Menu highlight is alpha on the accent, not a token that was never defined
why: bg-pk-accent-wash named a token this theme has never had, so it generated no CSS and the keyboard-and-pointer cursor was a text colour change on nothing; the kit already tints with alpha elsewhere, so no new token was warranted
result: zero stylesheet rules mentioned accent-wash before; highlighted item now paints oklab(.../0.15) with white text while the rest stay transparent

decision: Fourteen prop types the components export were missing from the package entry
why: a consumer wrapping Menu.Item, Dialog.Close, Popover.Trigger or Toolbar.Group could not import the type for the part they were wrapping
evidence: src/index.ts for dialog, menu, popover and toolbar
result: the four blocks now re-export every type their component file declares

decision: ToggleGroup honours orientation; Accordion refuses it, superseding the open row below
why: the same audit, split by judgment rather than one blanket rule — a stacked filter rail is a real arrangement and costs one line, while a horizontal accordion animates width and rules the other edge, so it is a different component and styling one on spec is invention
result: the vertical group renders a 123px-tall column of four against the row's 27px; passing orientation to Accordion now fails the typecheck at disclosure.tsx:41, checked by adding it and removing it again

decision: Slider honours orientation, the third component with this fault
why: Root accepts orientation and every part carried data-orientation=vertical while the markup drew a 224 by 4 track lying on its side; a vertical control has no length of its own so it takes a default one, overridable through className
result: vertical now measures control 16x120, track 4x120, indicator 4x66 — and 66 of 120 is the 55 it was given; the four horizontal sliders are unchanged

decision: Three defects share one cause: a type that accepts a variation the markup was never written for
why: toolbar orientation, tabs orientation, slider arity and orientation all typechecked, rendered, and were wrong; none would have been found by reading a component alone, only by rendering the variation
result: the audit is now deliberate rather than incidental

decision: Accordion.Root accepts orientation and the kit styles only vertical
why: a horizontal accordion would render as a broken column, but this design's accordion is a ruled list of rows and styling a horizontal one is speculative — the honest fix is likely to narrow the kit's type so it cannot be asked for
result: found and not yet addressed; named as the next action rather than left silent

decision: Tabs parts read their own data-orientation, the same fault the toolbar had
why: Root accepts orientation=vertical but the list was a fixed row and the marker measured the active tab's width when the axis it needed was its height; Base UI publishes --active-tab-height and --active-tab-top alongside the width and left
result: vertical tabs went from a 63x1 underline on a row to a 1x23 bar on a column, travelling y 573, 600, 627 across the three tabs

decision: Switch and ToggleGroup do not share the slider's fault
why: both were suspected of the same hardcoded-child problem; a switch has exactly one thumb by definition and ToggleGroup passes its children through, so neither can under-render what its type accepts
result: no change made

decision: Slider renders one thumb per value
why: its props accept an array because they are Base UI's Root props, but the composition hardcoded a single thumb, so a range rendered a reachable minimum and an invisible maximum while the readout claimed both
result: a range of 24 and 68 rendered 1 thumb and 1 input before, 2 thumbs at x 592 and 690 with 2 inputs after; the three single-value sliders still render one each

decision: Overlay placement is demonstrated
why: side, align, sideOffset and alignOffset are props on every overlay in the kit and every instance used the defaults, so nothing on the page said placement could be set at all
result: the default popup sits below its trigger, 330 against a bottom of 322; side=right align=start sideOffset=10 puts it at x 384 against a trigger right of 375 with tops aligned to within a pixel

decision: Bars max is demonstrated on two series of one metric
why: bars scale to their own peak unless told otherwise, so a pair read as a comparison silently lies; max had never been used on the page
result: the smaller series draws 8px against the larger's 64px, a ratio of 0.125 against the true 510/4182 of 0.122; the auto-scaled chart above reaches the full 64px on a peak of 4182, which is what the small one would have drawn

decision: A shared ceiling would have been wrong on the existing pair
why: I framed this as two charts that cannot be compared, but they are installs and audio levels — different metrics, where independent scales are correct
result: left that pair alone and built the real case, one metric across two packages

decision: The vertical scroll area no longer traps content sideways
why: it overflowed horizontally with axis=vertical, so a strip of every commit line existed with no scrollbar to reach it; widening the box to fit the longest line is the fix, since a vertical-only area's content must only ever be too tall
result: overflowX measured 12px, then 20px, now 0; overflowY still 70

decision: The trapped strip was the text, not my padding
why: I removed pr-3 believing the gutter caused it and the overflow grew from 12 to 20px, which showed the cause was the line width all along
result: padding stayed off for its own reason — the bar is an overlay — but it was never the cause

decision: ScrollArea axis=both is demonstrated
why: only vertical had ever rendered, and a horizontal bar in a kit whose scrollbar hides until hover is where a silent layout fault would sit
result: both renders three children: a 4x56 vertical bar, a 182x4 horizontal bar and a 4x4 corner

decision: The level bounds are demonstrated, not just available
why: I added thresholds without showing it, so the one prop that stops a non-commit series collapsing into one colour was invisible on the page that documents the component
result: a minutes series over 18 weeks spreads 26/61/31/8 across four levels; on the defaults every non-zero value clears the top bound, which the test file already pins

decision: A props table cannot be derived for non-variant props
why: label, showValue, axis, side and sideOffset are TypeScript interface props, not tv variants, so nothing can read them at runtime; hand-listing them is the drift the derived table exists to avoid
result: demonstrating them on the page instead, starting with thresholds

decision: Every page imports through the package entry, superseding the one-page row below
why: proving the barrel on one page left most of the published surface — Bars, ActivityGrid, IconTile, Surface, Switch, Slider, Tabs, Accordion, Collapsible, ScrollArea, Separator, Toolbar — still exercised by nothing
result: all seven pages render off "polkadot-ui" with zero failed requests

decision: Dropped the #/* internal alias
why: nothing used it once the lab imported the kit by name, and src re-exports by relative path
result: removing it left typecheck, tests and the running app unchanged, which is what proves it was dead

decision: One page imports through the package entry, the way a consumer would
why: every page reached for the component files directly, so the published barrel was proven by nothing and a broken export would have surfaced only to the first outside user
result: the page renders through "polkadot-ui" — four sections, five buttons — and the dot-notation statics survive the barrel: menu group label, four items, a shortcut, a separator, popover title and close

decision: The popover showcases its Close part
why: PopoverClose was exported and demonstrated nowhere, and a close button is also the one dismissal that does not depend on focus management
result: clicking it takes the trigger's aria-expanded from true to false

decision: Escape and outside-press cannot be verified in this pane
why: opening a popover leaves focus on BODY because document.hidden stops Base UI's focus management running, and its dismissal is bound inside the floating context, so the key never reaches a handler; the popup also stays mounted after closing because the exit transition never completes
evidence: live DOM, docHidden true, activeElement BODY, focusInsidePopup false
result: toggling the trigger does close it — aria-expanded true to false to true — so the state machine is sound; no code changed

decision: The front door shows a composed widget, not only prose about one
why: the overview explained the kit in four text cards and never showed it building anything; a component library's first screen should answer what the parts are for
result: one Surface holding Kind, Meta, Title, Prose, Label, Readout, Bars, three IconTiles, a Separator and a Button — 360x303, four Rows, no new css

decision: Row wraps once its two ends stop fitting
why: metadata is nowrap because it is short by nature, so a Row that cannot wrap pushes its right end out of whatever contains it — clipped inside a Surface, out of the column on a page; nothing moves while both ends fit
result: at 825 all seven two-child rows still sit on one line; at 560 no row overflows and the body does not scroll sideways

decision: The hairline rules are 150px and their row wraps, superseding the 220px row above
why: my own earlier fix caused this: a fixed 220px rule beside a mono caption ran past the card, and Surface clips, so "a rule inside a card" rendered as "a rule inside a car"
result: measured 3px of overflow before, zero after, four rules still equal

decision: Section captions are metadata again, not sentences
why: six captions across four pages were 41 to 55 characters set in a nowrap mono role meant for "371 days" and "04"; one was wider than the whole column, which no amount of wrapping can seat
evidence: app/routes on foundations, layout, overlays, data
result: zero overflowing children across all seven pages at a 560px viewport

decision: theme.css scans the kit's own components
why: Tailwind only emits a class it has seen, and every class the kit uses lives in a tv call inside the package, not in the consumer's source; without it a consumer imports the tokens, gets no error, and renders everything unstyled
result: the app's own @source was deleted and all seven pages stay styled with zero missing classes, so the scan is the kit's and not the app's

decision: Removed motion, which nothing imported
why: the runtime confirms it — zero motion modules loaded while Base UI and tailwind-variants are — and the repo prefers deletion to speculative machinery; no component needs a spring or FLIP until a board exists
result: app still renders after the install; the spring constants and motion findings stay in this trail, so it returns in one command

decision: No other kit class names a token the theme never defined
why: three such bugs have shipped here — the pill radius, the activity levels, and now the menu highlight — and Tailwind drops an unknown utility silently, so the class had to be swept rather than trusted
evidence: every pk- class rendered across the seven pages, checked against the class names the stylesheet actually defines
result: clean on all seven; an earlier run flagged pk-rim, which was my regex taking the comma in ".pk-rim, .pk-rim-tile" as part of the name

decision: MenuSeparator forwards its props
why: it accepted only className and dropped everything else, unlike every other part in the file
result: typechecks against Base UI's Separator props

decision: ScrollArea needed no change
why: I expected the hidden-until-hover scrollbar to leave keyboard users stranded; Base UI already gives the viewport tabIndex 0 when content overflows, so the kit's focus ring applies and arrows scroll
evidence: live DOM, scrollHeight 132 against clientHeight 62, tabIndex 0
result: no code changed; the hidden gutter is a documented design decision and not a defect

decision: Toolbar parts read their own data-orientation instead of a variant
why: the orientation variant reached only the root, so Group and Separator called toolbar() with no argument and a vertical rail kept horizontal groups and upright dividers; the vertical rules in the variant were unreachable and looked correct
result: vertical rail now has a column group 20x44 and a 16x1 rule, horizontal keeps a row group and a 1x16 divider

decision: ActivityGrid takes its level bounds as a prop
why: the ladder 1/3/6/10 fits commits per day, the only series the design showed; any other series — minutes, degrees, messages — collapsed into one colour with no way to say otherwise
result: minutes [0,12,45,90,240] read 0,4,4,4,4 on the defaults and 0,1,2,3,4 on their own bounds

decision: Levels count the bounds a value clears, replacing a ternary ladder
why: nested ternaries are banned in this repo and the chain also hard-coded exactly four levels
result: equivalence checked over counts 0-40 against the old ladder; live grid still 45/81/50/6 across 182 cells

decision: Bars does not hard-code thresholds, contrary to what I said when naming this work
why: it already takes max and minHeight; only ActivityGrid had baked-in bounds
result: no change made to Bars

decision: IconTile, the design's most repeated shape, was missing
why: fourteen skill tiles in the source, each a one-cell square widening to three and revealing a word; nothing else occurs half as often, and my earlier claim that the primitive set was complete missed it
result: five tiles measure 48px square, icon 26 plus padding 20 plus border 2; held open reaches 114 with a 66px label column

decision: The reveal column is minmax(0,0fr), not 0fr
why: a bare 0fr is minmax(auto,0fr), and that automatic minimum kept the label's own left padding alive as a nine-pixel sliver on every collapsed tile
result: collapsed column measured 9px before and 0px after; tiles are now exact squares

decision: ActivityGrid is a chart, not a data grid
why: it claimed role=grid over 182 gridcells with zero rows between them, which ARIA forbids, and no cell was focusable, so nothing could navigate what the markup asserted; the plot now says role=img once and the readout announces each day as the cursor moves
result: root group, zero stray grid/gridcell roles, label "182 days, Thu Mar 12 2026 to Wed Sep 09 2026, 344 in total", readout changes on every arrow

decision: The toolbar keyboard claim is accurate
why: the page states one tab stop and arrows between buttons, which had never been driven
result: tabindex 0,-1,-1,-1,-1 roves to -1,0,... then -1,-1,0,... and ArrowLeft returns; my first probe failed only because it kept dispatching from the button that had lost the roving index

decision: The published contrast table is accurate
why: the kit states measured ink-on-ground ratios in theme.css and repeats them on the foundations page, which would be a false accessibility claim if stale
evidence: recomputed WCAG sRGB from the live token values
result: all 18 ink/ground pairs match the published figures to the cent, zero drift, no change needed

decision: A type scale of nine sans steps and three mono steps, each carrying size, line height, tracking and weight
why: owner rejected the kit's type; every component carried its own four-part text-[13px] leading-[1.3] tracking-[-0.015em] font-medium, so a role could be wrong in one part and nothing showed it; values taken from the design source's own measured usage, not invented
result: a role is now one utility; 12 steps replace 20 near-duplicate hand-written triples

decision: Rebuilt the control language: fills instead of outlines, one 8px control radius, offset focus rings
why: owner: the controls are the part they most dislike, in the kit and in the design source both; wanted modern, clean, minimalist
result: rendered at /controls: four button tones read as one family, segmented track hugs its content, switch and slider lost their borders

decision: Mono is only for a value read as data; the interface is sans
why: owner: no monospace in controls; the rendered page showed mono was carrying the chrome as well — section descriptions, nav subtitle, filter status
result: before: every description line was DM Mono; after: sans, and mono survives only in the API table identifiers and Readout

decision: ToggleGroup root takes self-start
why: an inline-flex control is still stretched by a flex-column parent, so the segmented track spanned the full 528px content width instead of hugging its three choices
result: rendered: track is now the width of 3m/6m/max

decision: The design's composite cards are the library, not app code
why: owner: "there's a bunch missing ... basically all of these" over the full design render; the kit had 21 Base UI wrappers and none of the shapes the design is actually made of
result: starting the composites, most-repeated shape first

decision: Sparkline: SVG trace, HTML head
why: drawn three times in the design, more than any other data shape; the source draws it on canvas with a live feed, which a component library cannot ship
result: rendered at /data across three series shapes: drifting, noisy with an excursion, and flat against a ceiling

decision: d3-shape owns the line, the area and the monotone curve
why: the design's trace is a monotone cubic through its samples; hand-rolling that interpolation is the case the no-hand-rolling rule exists for
result: kit runtime deps go from 2 to 3; d3-shape tree-shakes to the three functions used

decision: Badge, Breakdown and Stat
why: the design's largest card is a repo card, and it needs a standing label, a proportion bar with a legend and figure-plus-word pairs; the badge shape alone appears six times
result: the repo card now renders end to end at / : public badge, 84/9/7 language bar, four stats, commit trace

decision: The overview's mono house rule was false after the type change
why: it still told readers mono metadata is the kit's default text role, which the same session had just reversed; a document that overclaims is a defect
result: replaced with the rule that now holds: sans is the interface, mono is a value

decision: Avatar and StatusDot are components after all
why: an earlier count of the design source refuted both; the full render shows an initials tile twice and a pulsing status mark on the identity card, so the count was wrong
result: the identity card renders at / : rim tile, name, role, live mark

decision: Base UI owns Avatar, so the kit wraps it rather than writing one
why: its Fallback holds until the image resolves, which is the part that is easy to get wrong — initials must not flash behind a picture that loads at once
result: no load-state code in the kit; radius steps with size so a small tile is not a circle

decision: Receipt, in parts
why: the theme has carried the paper ground, the dotted rule and the tear clip since the first commit and nothing used them; no two receipts hold the same rows, so it is composed rather than taken whole
result: computed styles confirm tear clip-path, paper gradient, ink #2b2b28, dotted rule, 18 bars in two widths, dashed action

decision: Print is a fourth type register
why: a receipt is a printed object at 9 to 12.5px, below every interface step; reusing the interface scale would have meant magic numbers back in the slots
result: two steps, both taken from the design source's receipt

decision: tailwind-merge was deleting every slot colour that sat beside a font size
why: it cannot tell text-pk-label from text-pk-on-accent and keeps one; the icon button set no size, so only its glyph kept the colour, which is what the owner saw
result: measured after: all four solid buttons rgb(4,17,11) at 11.5px/11.5px, was rgb(237,237,237) at 16px/24px for the icon

decision: No prose comments in the source; short JSDoc on public props only
why: owner rule
result: every block comment removed, vp check clean on 45 files

result: breakdownShares drops a share that is not a positive number, and the same fractions feed both the bar and the legend so the two cannot disagree

decision: The layout preview takes percentages, not fractions
why: the props table added two commits ago said fractions; the component's own JSDoc says percentages of the frame, and the fixture passes 6, 8, 40, 84
evidence: read the fixture against the interpolation
result: the row now says percentages; the geometry was left alone, since the frame clips and no natural input reaches it

decision: The accent had a fallback that was never wired up
why: --pk-accent was a display-p3 colour with --pk-accent-srgb sitting unused beneath it; where p3 is unsupported that value is invalid at computed-value time, so the accent does not fall back to sRGB, it disappears
evidence: on this browser the token and the painted background are both the p3 value, unchanged
result: the sRGB hex is the base and an @supports block raises it to p3, so the colour survives a browser that lacks p3 instead of vanishing

decision: A component could draw with a token the theme never declared
why: a class like bg-pk-surface-raised compiles, lints and renders as nothing; there was no check that a token exists
evidence: renamed a real class in badge.tsx and watched the test report it by class and by file
result: a test maps every Tailwind prefix to its @theme namespace and compares; 80 references across 38 components, all declared

decision: The theme has no dead surface
why: four raw variables and one class were declared and referenced nowhere; two of them were board layout tokens my own grid change had already superseded
evidence: scanned declarations against every reference in src and app
result: pk-face, --pk-surface-face, --pk-duration-feed, --pk-board-gap and --pk-board-columns removed; 78 raw variables and 131 tokens all in use

decision: The rest of the theme's modern CSS degrades
why: the accent's failure raised the question for everything else that a browser can refuse: @property, scroll-driven animation, color-mix
evidence: every var(--pk-rim) site carries a 140deg fallback; the glow's color-mix is decorative; a probe without animation-timeline computed duration 0s and opacity 1, which is pk-rise's end state
result: the accent was the only one that failed closed, because a declaration cannot carry a fallback the way var() can

decision: The documented setup line is the one the app runs
why: the README told a consumer to import polkadot-ui/theme.css while the app imported a relative path, so the documented entry had never been executed
evidence: switched the app to the package specifier: ground #08090a, Schibsted Grotesk, card #0e0f11, radius 16px, all unchanged
result: @source "." still resolves through the export, so the instruction is proven rather than asserted

decision: A component nobody demonstrates is invisible
why: an unexported component fails the app's typecheck, because every page imports from the package; an exported one that no page renders fails nothing and is documented nowhere
evidence: all 90 exported components are rendered on a page today
result: a test reads each component's own Tabs.Tab = Tab declarations for the JSX name, rather than guessing one from the shape of the export

decision: The coverage guard checked four fifths of the surface and looked complete
why: the entry writes some exports on one line and some over several, and the first rule only matched the multi-line shape, so Button, Surface, Row, Badge and 14 more were never examined
evidence: counted 72 seen against 90 exported, then added an alias nobody renders and watched it still pass
result: both shapes and the X as Y form are parsed now; the injected alias fails by name, and the floor asserts 85 rather than 50

decision: The rest of the entry point is sound
why: no component module is left out, and every variant object and props type reaches it
evidence: scanned all 39 modules against the entry
result: nothing to fix; the pure helpers extracted for tests stay module-only on purpose, and the test does not ask for them

decision: A pill lifts its own background, and the token page cannot see it
why: foundations measures ink against surface, so ink-faint reads 4.95; inside the feed's duration pill the 6% ink background raises the floor and the same ink lands at 4.40, under AA
evidence: measured every text node against its composited background on all eight routes: 871 elements, one failure
result: the pill takes ink-dim, 5.03 on its own background, which is one step up and leaves the chip as quiet as it was

decision: The first contrast probe read oklab as rgb
why: Tailwind emits oklab() for an alpha colour, and taking the first three numbers made a near-white label measure as near-black; it reported four failures, all false, including an aurora label that is really 8.91
evidence: filled a 1x1 canvas with each colour and read the pixel back, which lets the browser do the conversion
result: the audit composites through every ancestor background the same way, so a translucent layer counts

decision: Text on a gradient is measured by hand, not by the sweep
why: the sweep skips an element whose background is an image, because it cannot flatten one; that is the receipt's paper and the aurora
evidence: receipt ink 13.48 to 12.03 and label 5.76 to 5.14 measured earlier; aurora label 8.91
result: the exclusion is deliberate and the excluded set is small enough to name

decision: One button tone disabled itself differently from the other three
why: solid swaps to a flat treatment and lands at 4.68; soft, outline and ghost set the faintest ink and then halved it again with opacity-50, landing at 2.01
evidence: measured all four as rendered, opacity included: 4.68, 2.01, 2.10, 2.10
result: the double dim is gone, so all four sit at 4.68 to 5.14 and read as one state; WCAG exempts an inactive control either way, this was consistency

decision: Every interactive state clears AA
why: the sweep measured default states only, and hover and selection change both colours at once
evidence: menu 12.01 normal and 14.15 highlighted, solid button 12.75, pressed toggle 18.45; ten hover pairs from 8.16 to 19.18, including the receipt action inverting to 13.48
result: nothing to fix; the accent-backed states are the ones that could have been wrong and are the strongest

decision: The contrast sweep is blind to element opacity
why: it reads colour and background but not a parent's opacity, so a halved element measures as if it were solid
evidence: every fractional-opacity element on all eight routes is either disabled, which WCAG exempts, or has no text
result: no failure is hidden today; the sweep lives in a session rather than the suite, because it needs a real browser

decision: An accent focus ring on paper is invisible
why: the receipt's action button is the one control on the light ground, and it had no ring of its own; the kit's accent ring measures 1.21 against paper, which is not a ring
evidence: measured the accent at both opacities on four grounds, and paper ink on both ends of the paper gradient
result: the action takes a paper-ink ring at 12.03 to 13.48; every other ring stays accent

decision: The focus ring had two opacities for no reason
why: six components rang the accent at 45 percent and five at 50, which is drift rather than a decision
evidence: 45 measures 3.31 against the 3:1 that non-text needs, 50 measures 3.78
result: standardised on 50, the one with margin, rather than on 45, which six of eleven used; the count did not decide it

decision: The ring offsets are two groups on purpose
why: five standalone controls carry a ring offset and five rows inside cards do not, which reads as drift until you see which is which
evidence: button, slider, switch, tabs and toggle group sit on a ground; accordion, collapsible, icon tile, scroll area and the nav link sit inside a card, where an offset would cut the neighbour
result: left as it is; only the colour was unified

decision: The injected stylesheet keeps utilities the source has dropped
why: after the change the page still contained the 45 percent ring and the sheet was byte-identical across a reload, which looks like the edit failing
evidence: fetched the stylesheet from the dev server with no-store: 45 absent, 50 and the paper ring present
result: read generated CSS from the server, not from document.styleSheets, which accumulates across hot updates
